title: Tomato Bruschetta
description: Charred toast rubbed with raw garlic and piled with salted ripe tomatoes, basil and good olive oil. It is only as good as the tomatoes, so make it in summer.

steps.text: Cut the tomatoes into roughly 1 cm dice, discarding the hard cores. Toss with the salt in a sieve set over a bowl and leave to drain.
steps.tip: Salting draws out the watery juice so the flavour is concentrated and the toast stays crisp.

steps.text: Tip the drained tomatoes into a bowl and stir in the 2 tbsp of olive oil, the vinegar if your tomatoes need sharpening, and a grind of black pepper. Tear in the basil. Taste and add more salt if needed.
Heat a griddle pan over a high heat or turn the grill to its highest setting. Toast the bread until crisp and charred in places on the outside but still a little chewy within, 1–2 minutes each side.
While the toast is hot, rub one side of each slice with the cut face of the garlic — the rough surface acts as a grater — then drizzle with the remaining oil.
steps.tip: Two or three firm strokes per slice is plenty. Raw garlic is strong and it should sit in the background.

steps.text: Spoon the tomatoes onto the toasts and serve immediately, before the bread softens.

tips: Never use tomatoes straight from the fridge; cold mutes their flavour. Leave them out for at least an hour first.
The salty tomato juice left in the bowl is too good to waste. Whisk it into a salad dressing.

substitutions.note: quartered; usually the best choice outside high summer

storage: Assemble just before eating. The dressed tomatoes will keep, covered at room temperature, for up to 2 hours; add the basil at the last minute.
author: Simmer
